text: Let $x^{k} + y^{k} = a^{k}, (a, k > 0 )$ and $\frac{dy}{dx}+\left (\frac{y}{x}\right )^{\frac{1}{3}}=0$, then k is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$x^{k} + y^{k} = a^{k}$

$\Rightarrow$ $kx^{k - 1} + ky^{k - 1}\frac{dy}{dx}$ = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{dy}{dx}+\left (\frac{x}{y}\right )^{k-1}$ = 0 ...(1)

Given $\frac{dy}{dx}+\left (\frac{y}{x}\right )^{\frac{1}{3}}=0$ ...(2)

Comparing (1) and (2), we get

k - 1 = $-\frac{1}{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ k = $\frac{2}{3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

  then the matrix
$A^{31}$ is equal to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$x^{2} + x + 1 = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ x = $\frac{-1+i\sqrt{3}}{2}$ = $ω$ or $\frac{-1-i\sqrt{3}}{2}$ = $ω^{2}$

Let $α$ = $ω$

$\therefore$ A = $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & ω & ω^{2} \\ 1 & ω^{2} & ω^{4} \end{array}\right ]$

$A^{2} =$ $\frac{1}{3}\left [\begin{array}{lll} 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \end{array}\right ]$ = $\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \end{array}\right ]$

Now $A^{4} =$ $\left [\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array}\right ]$ = I

$\therefore$ $A^{31} = A^{28}A^{3} = A^{3}$

text:
Let $α$ and $β$ be two real roots of the equation 
$(k + 1)\tan ^{2}x -$ $\sqrt{2}$ . $λ$tanx = (1 - k), where k($\neq$ - 1)
and $λ$ are real numbers. if $\tan ^{2} (α$ + $β$) = 50, then a value of $λ$ is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let tan$α$ and tan$β$ are the roots of

$(k + 1)\tan ^{2}x -$ $\sqrt{2}$ . $λ$tanx - (1 - k) = 0

$\therefore$ tan$α$ + tan$β$ = $\frac{\sqrt{2}λ}{k+1}$

and tan$α$.tan$β$ = $\frac{k-1}{k+1}$

Now tan($α$ + $β$)

= $\frac{\tan α+\tan β}{1-\tan α\tan β}$

= $\frac{\frac{λ\sqrt{2}}{k+1}}{1-\frac{k-1}{k+1}}$

= $\frac{λ\sqrt{2}}{2}$ = $\frac{λ}{\sqrt{2}}$

Given $\frac{λ^{2}}{2}$ = 50

$\Rightarrow$ $λ$ = 10

text: A vector $\vec{a}=α\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+β\widehat{k}(α,β\in R)$ lies in the plane of the vectors, $\vec{b}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}$ and  $\vec{c}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+4\widehat{k}$. If $\vec{a}$ bisects the angle between $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$, then:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Angle bisector $\vec{a}=λ\left (\hat{b}+\hat{c}\right )$

= $λ\left (\frac{\hat{i}+\hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{\hat{i}-\hat{j}+4\widehat{k}}{3\sqrt{2}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\vec{a}=\frac{λ}{3\sqrt{2}}\left (4\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+4\widehat{k}\right )$

comparing with $\vec{a}=α\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+β\widehat{k}$

$\frac{2λ}{3\sqrt{2}}$ = 2

$\Rightarrow$ $λ$ = $3\sqrt{2}$

$\therefore$ $\vec{a}=\left (4\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+4\widehat{k}\right )$

Then $\vec{a}.\widehat{k}-4$

= 4 - 4 = 0

text: If $\mathrm{Re}\left (\frac{z-1}{2z+i}\right )=1$, where z = x + iy, then the point (x, y) lies on a :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{Re}\left (\frac{z-1}{2z+i}\right )=1$

Put z = x + iy

$\therefore$ $\mathrm{Re}\left (\frac{(x+iy)-1}{2(x+iy)+i}\right )=1$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{Re}\left (\left (\frac{(x-1)+iy}{2x+i(2y+1)}\right )\left (\frac{2x-i(2y+1)}{2x-i(2y+1)}\right )\right )=1$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{Re}\left (\frac{\{(x-1)+iy\}\{2x-i(2y+1)\}}{4x^{2}+(2y+1)^{2}}\right )=1$

Real part of this equation is  = 1

$\therefore$ $\frac{2x(x-1)+y(2y+1)}{4x^{2}+(2y+1)^{2}}$ = 1

$\Rightarrow$ $2x^{2} + 2y^{2} +2x + 3y + 1 = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ $x^{2} + y^{2} +x +$ $\frac{3}{2}$y + $\frac{1}{2}$ = 0

This is an equation of circle. 

$\therefore$ Locus is a circle whose

center is $\left (-\frac{1}{2},-\frac{3}{4}\right )$ and radius $\frac{\sqrt{5}}{4}$

$\therefore$ Diameter = 2 $\times$ $\frac{\sqrt{5}}{4}$ = $\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

text: Total number of 6-digit numbers in which only and all the five digits 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 appear, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Here exactly one of the five digits appears twice.

We can choose the number which repeats more than once among 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 in $^{5}C_{1}$ ways.

Let number 3 repeats more than once. So six digits are 1, 3, 3, 5, 7, 9.

We can arrange those six digits in $\frac{6!}{2!}$ ways.

$\therefore$ Total six digit numbers $= ^{5}C_{1}$ $\times$ $\frac{6!}{2!}$ = $\frac{5}{2}(6!)$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

text:
If the distance between the foci of an ellipse is 6 and the distance between its directrices is 12,
then the length of its latus rectum is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Distance between foci = 2ae = 6

$\Rightarrow$ ae = 3 .....(1)

Distance between directrices = $\frac{2a}{e}$ = 12

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{a}{e}$ = 6 .....(2)

from (1) and (2) 

$a^{2} = 18$

also $a^{2}e^{2} = 9$

$\Rightarrow$ $18e^{2} = 9$

$\Rightarrow$ $e^{2} =$ $\frac{1}{2}$

We know $e^{2} = 1 -$ $\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{2}$ = 1 - $\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $b^{2} = 9$

$\therefore$ Length of latus rectum = $\frac{2b^{2}}{a}$

= $\frac{2\times 9}{\sqrt{18}}$

= $3\sqrt{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

text:
An unbiased coin is tossed 5 times. Suppose that a variable X is assigned the value of k when k
consecutive heads are obtained for k = 3, 4, 5, otherwise X takes the value -1. Then the expected
value of X, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Number of ways 3 consecutive heads can appers

(1) HHHT$_$

$(2) _$THHH

(3) THHHT

$\therefore$ Probablity of getting 3 consecutive heads

= $\frac{2}{32}$ + $\frac{2}{32}$ + $\frac{1}{32}$ = $\frac{5}{32}$

Number of ways 4 consecutive heads can appers

(1) HHHHT

(2) THHHH

$\therefore$ Probablity of getting 4 consecutive heads

= $\frac{1}{32}$ + $\frac{1}{32}$ = $\frac{2}{32}$

Number of ways 5 consecutive heads can appers

(1) HHHHH

$\therefore$ Probablity of getting 5 consecutive heads

= $\frac{1}{32}$

Now Probablity of getting 0, 1, and 2 consecutive heads

= 1 - $\left (\frac{5}{32}+\frac{2}{32}+\frac{1}{32}\right )$ = $\frac{24}{32}$

Now, Expectation

= (-1) $\times$ $\frac{24}{32}$ + 3 $\times$ $\frac{5}{32}$ + 4 $\times$ $\frac{2}{32}$ + 5 $\times$ $\frac{1}{32}$

= $\frac{1}{8}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

text:
If ƒ(a + b + 1 - x) = ƒ(x), for all x, where a and b are fixed positive real numbers, then

$\frac{1}{a+b}\int\limits _{a}^{b}x(f(x)+f(x+1))dx$ is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Replacing $x$ by $x+1$ in $f(a+b+1-x)=f(x)$ gives $f(a+b-x)=f(x+1)$.

Denote the given expression by $I$, so that

$(a+b)I=\int\limits _{a}^{b}x\{f(x)+f(x+1)\}dx$

Replacing $x$ by $a+b-x$ and using $f(a+b-x)=f(x+1)$ and $f(a+b+1-x)=f(x)$:

$(a+b)I=\int\limits _{a}^{b}(a+b-x)\{f(x+1)+f(x)\}dx$

Adding the two forms:

$2(a+b)I=(a+b)\int\limits _{a}^{b}\{f(x)+f(x+1)\}dx\Rightarrow 2I=\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(x)dx+\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(x+1)dx$

Since $\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(x+1)dx=\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(a+b-x)dx=\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(x)dx$, this gives

$I=\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(x)dx=\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(x+1)dx$

Option (A): with $x+1=t$, $\int\limits _{a-1}^{b-1}f(x+1)dx=\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(t)dt=I$.

Option (D): with $x=t+1$, $\int\limits _{a+1}^{b+1}f(x)dx=\int\limits _{a}^{b}f(t+1)dt=I$.

Options (B) and (C) are not equal to $I$ in general: for $a=1$, $b=2$ and $f(x)=(x-2)^{2}$, which satisfies $f(4-x)=f(x)$, $I=\dfrac{1}{3}$ while each of (B) and (C) equals $\dfrac{7}{3}$.

Hence, the correct options are (A) and (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

text:
If the system of linear equations

2x + 2ay + az = 0

2x + 3by + bz = 0

2x + 4cy + cz = 0,

where a, b, c $\in$ R are non-zero distinct; has a non-zero solution, then:
options: a, b, c are in G.P.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For non-zero solution

$\left |\begin{array}{lll} 2 & 2a & a \\ 2 & 3b & b \\ 2 & 4c & c \end{array}\right |=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & 2a & a \\ 0 & 3b-2a & b-a \\ 0 & 4c-2a & c-a \end{array}\right |=0$

$\Rightarrow$  (3b – 2a) (c –a) – (b – a) (4c – 2a) = 0

$\Rightarrow$ 2ac = bc + ab

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{2}{b}=\frac{1}{a}+\frac{1}{c}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{a},\frac{1}{b},\frac{1}{c}$ are in A.P.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

If $y(α)=\sqrt{2\left (\frac{\tan α+\cot α}{1+\tan ^{2}α}\right )+\frac{1}{\sin ^{2}α}},α\in \left (\frac{3π}{4},π\right )$

$\frac{dy}{dα}atα=\frac{5π}{6}is$ :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$y(α)=\sqrt{2\left (\frac{\tan α+\cot α}{1+\tan ^{2}α}\right )+\frac{1}{\sin ^{2}α}}$

= $\sqrt{2\left (\frac{1+\tan ^{2}α}{\tan α\left (1+\tan ^{2}α\right )}\right )+\frac{1}{\sin ^{2}α}}$

= $\sqrt{2\left (\frac{\cos α}{\sin α}\right )+\frac{1}{\sin ^{2}α}}$

= $\sqrt{\frac{\sin 2α+1}{\sin ^{2}α}}$

= $\frac{|\sin α+\cos α|}{|\sin α|}$

At $α$ = $\frac{5π}{6}$

$|\sin α+\cos α|$ = -(sin$α$ + cos$α$)

and |sin$α$| = sin$α$

$\therefore$ y($α$) = $\frac{-(\sin α+\cos α)}{\sin α}$

= -1 - cot$α$

$\therefore$ $\frac{dy}{dα}$ = cosec$^{2}α$

So $\frac{dy}{dα}$ at $α$ = $\frac{5π}{6}$,

= cosec$^{2}\frac{5π}{6}$ = 4
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

text:
If y = y(x) is the solution of the differential equation, $e^{y}\left (\frac{dy}{dx}-1\right )=e^{x}$ such that y(0) = 0, then
y(1) is equal to:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,
 $e^{y}\left (\frac{dy}{dx}-1\right )=e^{x}$

$\Rightarrow$ $e^{y}\frac{dy}{dx}-e^{y}=e^{x}$ ....(1)

Let $e^{y}=t$ $\Rightarrow$ $e^{y}\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{dt}{dx}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{dt}{dx}-t=e^{x}$

So here p = -1 and $q = e^{x}$

We know, IF = $e^{\int pdx}$

= $e^{\int -1dx}$ = $e^{-x}$

$\therefore$ t.$e^{-x}$ = $\int e^{x}.e^{-x}dx$

$\Rightarrow$ t.$e^{-x}$ = x + c

Putting value of t, we get

$e^{y}e^{-x}$ = x + c

$\Rightarrow$ $e^{y-x}=x+c$ .....(2)

Given y(0) = 0 means y = 0 when x = 0.

Putting in equation (2), we get

$e^{0} = 0 + c$

$\Rightarrow$ c = 1

$\therefore$ $e^{y-x}=x+1$ ....(3)

Now we have to find y(1), which means when x = 1 find the value of y in the above equation.

Putting x = 1 in equation (3)

$e^{y-1}=1+1$

$\Rightarrow$ $y - 1 = \log _{e}2$

$\Rightarrow$ $y = 1 + \log _{e}2$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

text: Five numbers are in A.P. whose sum is 25 and product is 2520. If one of these five numbers is -$\frac{1}{2}$ , then the greatest number amongst them is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the A.P is

a - 2d, a - d, a, a + d, a + 2d

$\because$ sum = 25 
$\Rightarrow$  5a = 25 $\Rightarrow$ a = 5

Also given,

 product $(a^{2} – 4d^{2}) (a^{2} – d^{2}).a = 2520$

$\Rightarrow$ $(25 – 4d^{2}) (25 –d^{2})5 = 2520$

$\Rightarrow$ $4d^{4}$
 $– 121d^{2}$
 $– 4d^{2}$
 + 121 = 0

$\Rightarrow$ $(d^{2}$
 $– 1) (4d^{2} – 121) = 0$

$\Rightarrow$ d = $\pm$1, d = $\pm \frac{11}{2}$

When d = $\pm$1 we can't get any fraction term like -$\frac{1}{2}$.

$\therefore$ d = $\pm \frac{11}{2}$

And when d = $\frac{11}{2}$

we get largest term = 5 + 2d = 5 + 11 = 16

text:
If the variance of the first n natural numbers is 10 and the variance of the first m even natural
numbers is 16, then m + n is equal $to_____$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Variance $σ^{2}=\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{N}-μ^{2}$

variance of (1, 2, ….. n)

10 = $\frac{1^{2}+2^{2}+....+n^{2}}{n}-\left (\frac{1+2+3+....+n}{n}\right )^{2}$

on solving we get n = 11

variance of 2, 4, 6…….2m = 16

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{2^{2}+4^{2}+....+(2m)^{2}}{m}-(m+1)^{2}$ = 16

$\Rightarrow$ $m^{2} = 49$

$\Rightarrow$ m = 7

$\therefore$ m + n = 18
